title: Homework: do non-ASCII digit strings actually occur in the real data?
spec: READ-ONLY. The single biggest unmeasured qualifier on T-3's failed correctness run. T-3 proved 'this CAN happen' - the Unicode-digit coercion gap makes float('１２３') read as 123.0 in Python and NULL in SQL - but never measured whether such strings occur in Evan's real data, so it did NOT prove 'this WILL happen to you'. Two parts: (1) a read-only sweep of the real GIMS data for strings containing non-ASCII digit characters, extending T-1's magnitude sweep to look INSIDE strings, reporting prevalence per collection; (2) a one-question inventory - is anything other than the GIMS Python process ever going to write rows autoSQL reads? Touches nothing, writes nothing, hours of work. This decides how good the other options look: if non-ASCII digits turn out to be COMMON, T-3's chosen fix converts silent wrong numbers into frequent visible refusals, and abandoning or narrowing the language become the honest choices instead.
